note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for treatment planning following confirmed high-grade prostate cancer and rapidly rising PSA.

Recently retired plumber with a history of prostate cancer diagnosis, currently presenting for treatment decision after biopsy confirmation. The patient is married and lives with his partner, who serves as his primary contact. He maintains a sedentary lifestyle with occasional walking and consumes approximately one unit of alcohol weekly. Recent outpatient appointments include cataract review in ophthalmology, knee follow-up in orthopaedics, and actinic keratosis check in dermatology. No current medications or known allergies. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 4/35. There are no comorbidities recorded, and he is a non-smoker.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth, symmetric, and non-nodular, consistent with clinical T stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs, including blood pressure 136/86 mmHg and heart rate 69 bpm. No lymphadenopathy or signs of metastatic disease are noted.
